new_findings.kind: security (asset gate hides a URL; same class as R5/R6: the crate's text differs from the browser's text before CSS tokenizing)
new_findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-web/src/assets.rs:567-575 (CDATA arm: inner.to_owned() with no input-stream preprocessing), :580 (concatenation with the now-preprocessed text pieces from :563), :586-588 (css over the joined text); cssurl.rs:163-170 (backslash + CR LF is one line continuation); lib.rs:43 DESCRIPTOR assets.scanned 'svg/math: the child text content, decoded text nodes and CDATA sections concatenated'
new_findings.evidence:
Payload: <svg><style>:root{b:"x\<![CDATA[]]>
;background:url(https://evil.example/p.png)}</style></svg> ( = raw CR byte, 
 = raw LF byte). The browser preprocesses the input stream first (CR followed by ']' becomes LF; 13.2.3.5), so the CDATA data is LF. The style's child text is :root{b:"x\ LF LF ;background:url(...)}. CSS reads backslash+LF as a continuation; the second LF ends the string as a bad-string; then url(https://evil.example/p.png) is a url token in a valid declaration and is loaded. The crate joins text ':root{b:"x' + raw CDATA '' + text '
;background:...'. cssurl::string treats backslash + CR LF as one continuation, so the string runs to EOF and swallows the url(). collect_assets reports nothing and the URL is neither denied nor offered to the port. The same happens with two CDATA sections ('<![CDATA[]]><![CDATA[
...]]>') or with a comment between the pieces. Text pieces are fine since 6d1c591 (text_value preprocesses each slice, and every slice ends before '<'). Only CDATA inner text is passed through raw. The shape was already present at R7, but this round's D5/D7 class (input-stream preprocessing) covers it. The V4-06 regex of the lane does not match the CDATA arm, so the 97-site sweep could not list it. The difftest comparator preprocesses CDATA itself (model.rs:68-79) and does not model the gate's CSS join, so it cannot see this.
new_findings.remediation: Apply input-stream newline preprocessing (CR LF and lone CR become LF; U+0000 may stay because CSS maps it to U+FFFD) to the CDATA inner text before joining. Do not decode character references: CDATA has none. Add V4-08 tests: the payload above (escape), CR-ended CDATA followed by a comment and then an LF-led text (decoy), and CR LF and CR CR LF variants plus two CDATA sections (case/whitespace). Each must report the URL as Denied(ExternalScheme). Widen the class regex with CDATA|strip_prefix\(OPEN and re-list the sites. Correct the DESCRIPTOR assets.decoding wording ('foreign style text with the text rules' is now the foreign-content rules).

new_findings.evidence: Lead asked (13:44:24Z) to confirm the gate still denies what it must. By reading: yes. classify (assets.rs:162-206) runs on the browser-identical value. U+FFFD is not trimmed as C0/space by either the crate or the URL parser, cannot start a valid scheme, and cannot form '//'. So '\0http://x' and 'java\0script:' are relative for both (same-origin path), '//e\0vil' is still ProtocolRelative, and 'http:\0//x' is still ExternalScheme. Only relative references with a NUL now reach the port as U+FFFD, which matches the browser. No test pins this change, though.
new_findings.remediation: Add a V4-08 test: reaches the port as 'a\u{fffd}b.png'; '\0//e.invalid/x', '//e\0.invalid/x' and 'ht\0tp://e.invalid' each give the decision above.

notes: The construction.rs detection rule matches the spec rows I checked (in body p/heading/form/li/dd/dt/button/a/nobr/select/input/hr/option/optgroup/ruby, in table/table body/row, column group start tags and text, head noscript, after head, after body). Scope and special sets are the spec lists or smaller (fail-closed). The one missed path is F2.

The current WHATWG tokenizer has processing instructions (13.2.5.72-.76: '<?target ...>' ends at the first '>'; the xml/xml-stylesheet targets and invalid targets become bogus comments; at EOF the PI is dropped). Tree builder modes insert PIs where they insert comments (initial/before html into the Document, after body into html, in column group, in table). The crate's opaque processing_instruction node has the same span and position, so there is no structure or gate impact. The DESCRIPTOR could name PIs as such (advisory).
Red proof and 56/56 green are recorded in the lane file (not re-run here, no cargo).
Lane status needs a decision before R9 (V4-14, see wip_note).

The oracle sink (oracle.rs) implements append_before_sibling / append_based_on_parent_node / reparent_children / add_attrs_if_missing / template contents in the shape html5ever expects. Data::Pi produces no event (oracle.rs:312) while the model maps '<?x>' to a Comment (model.rs:68-96). That only agrees because html5ever 0.40.1 still reads '<?' as a bogus comment. If html5ever adopts the PI tokenizer, the comments group will diverge (advisory).

D9 coverage is hand-written (60 restructuring + 32 accepted + 20 whole documents); the generator deliberately avoids restructuring tags. Neither group has </image> in colgroup (F2) or '</>' before a pre LF (F3). Most groups run in fragment mode with a div context, so skeleton/DOCTYPE behaviour is compared only in the whole-document group.

events::drop_implied removes attribute-less implied html/head/body/tbody/colgroup by count budget and alignment. I checked it on the F2 input: it would still report the colgroup mismatch, so N1 does not mask F2.

The asset gate's CSS reading (style_children join) is outside the comparator's event model, so F1 is invisible to the difftest by construction. A small gate-level differential (html5ever DOM text content of each style vs the crate's joined text) would cover that class.
